attribution_statements.quote: assess that cyber actors affiliated with the Russian General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 161st Specialist Training Center (Unit 29155) are responsible for computer network operations against global targets for the purposes of espionage, sabotage, and reputational harm
GRU Unit 29155 cyber actors began deploying the destructive WhisperGate malware against multiple Ukrainian victim organizations as early as January 13, 2022.
These cyber actors are separate from other known and more established GRU-affiliated cyber groups, such as Unit 26165 and Unit 74455.
attribution_statements.attributed_to: distinct from GRU Unit 26165 and Unit 74455

attribution_statements.quote: FBI, NSA, and CISA assess Unit 29155 is responsible for attempted coups, sabotage and influence operations, and assassination attempts throughout Europe.
FBI assesses the Unit 29155 cyber actors to be junior active-duty GRU officers under the direction of experienced Unit 29155 leadership.
FBI assesses Unit 29155 cyber actors rely on non-GRU actors, including known cyber-criminals and enablers to conduct their operations.
attribution_statements.attributed_to: non-GRU actors (known cyber-criminals and enablers) supporting Unit 29155

attribution_statements.quote: Note: Cybersecurity companies have different methods of tracking and attributing cyber actors, and this may not be a 1:1 correlation to the U.S. Government’s understanding for all activity related to these groupings.
attribution_statements.attributing_party: the authoring agencies (caveat on cybersecurity companies' tracking)
attribution_statements.attributed_to: industry group names (Cadet Blizzard, Ember Bear, Frozenvista, UNC2589, UAC-0056)

attribution_statements.quote: While Unit 29155 cyber actors are best known for their use of WhisperGate malware against Ukraine, the use of WhisperGate is not unique to the group.
attribution_statements.attributed_to: WhisperGate is not exclusive to Unit 29155

attribution_statements.quote: As a result, many TTPs overlap with those of other cyber actors, which can lead to misattribution.
For additional information on Russian state-sponsored malicious cyber activity

attribution_strength_rationale: FBI, CISA, and NSA 'assess that cyber actors affiliated with the Russian General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 161st Specialist Training Center (Unit 29155) are responsible for' the operations, and FBI 'assesses' them 'to be junior active-duty GRU officers'; a specific GRU unit is named with 'assess ... are responsible for' wording, so the 'affiliated with' hedge does not lower the code.

notes: (1) CVE-2020-1472, CVE-2021-26084, CVE-2021-3156, CVE-2021-4034 and CVE-2022-27666 are ones for which the actors obtained exploit scripts 'but not exploiting'; a model saying they were exploited is wrong. Only CVE-2021-33044, CVE-2021-33045, CVE-2022-26134, CVE-2022-26138 and CVE-2022-3236 were 'exploited ... for initial access'. (2) Unit 26165 and Unit 74455 are named only as SEPARATE, 'more established GRU-affiliated cyber groups'; listing them as aliases of Unit 29155 is wrong. (3) The industry names (Cadet Blizzard/DEV-0586, Ember Bear/Bleeding Bear, Frozenvista, UNC2589, UAC-0056) are 'related' names, with the caveat that they 'may not be a 1:1 correlation' to the U.S. Government's understanding. G1003 is a MITRE ATT&CK group ID. (4) The coups/sabotage/assassination sentence concerns Unit 29155's non-cyber operations in Europe. (5) WhisperGate use 'is not unique to the group'. Raspberry Robin use is hedged ('may have used ... in the role of an access broker'). Raspberry Robin and SaintBot were obtained via dark web forums. (6) The publicly available scanning tools carry a disclaimer: the actors were 'not observed using these tools outside of their intended purpose'. Nmap includes the Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE). secretsdump.py, psexec.py and ntlmrelayx.py are Impacket scripts. The GOST binary was named 'java'. EternalBlue is named without a CVE ID. VirusTotal and Shodan are online services used by the actors. (7) Not keyed as items: mega[.]nz (exfiltration domain, IOC), i.php/tunnel.jsp (resource names), port lists, Metasploit module names (mysql, postgres, ssh), VPS/VPN anonymization infrastructure, and generic 'reverse shell'. GitHub repositories are named only as the source of CVE exploit scripts (not an intrusion tool); SOCKS5 is the proxy mode GOST ran in (a protocol, not keyed separately). DEV-0586 is Microsoft's former name and Bleeding Bear is CrowdStrike's name. 'Russian state-sponsored' appears only in a pointer to DOJ press releases. Webmail and VPNs appear only in mitigation advice. (8) The DOJ press-release dates and February 26, 2022 are reference/publication dates, not activity dates. 'for 30 days' is a GOST usage duration, and 'more than 14,000 instances of domain scanning across at least 26 NATO members' is a count. (9) Not in the input: Appendix A (WhisperGate malware analysis), Tables 1-2 (victim observations, scripts) and Appendix B IOCs; component names that appear only there are not keyed. (10) No victims are named.
